questions.question: What is the difference between dragging text with the mouse (left-click) and Ctrl + dragging text in MS Word 365?

options.text: Dragging deletes the text; Ctrl + dragging pastes it.
Dragging moves the text; Ctrl + dragging copies it
Ctrl + dragging changes the font style

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dragging moves the text; Ctrl + dragging copies it**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dragging** text with the mouse (using left-click) moves the selected text from its original location to the target location.
 
• **Ctrl + dragging** text creates a copy of the selected text at the target location while retaining the original text at its original position.
 
• This functionality is useful for efficiently reorganizing or duplicating content within a document.
 
• Both actions involve selecting the text first and then using drag-and-drop techniques to reposition or duplicate it.
 
• These actions are part of the basic editing and formatting features in MS Word 365, enhancing user productivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drag-and-Drop Functionality:** A feature in MS Word that allows users to move or copy text by clicking and dragging without needing to use cut, copy, and paste commands.
 
• **Ctrl Key Modifier:** The Ctrl key acts as a modifier that changes the default behavior of drag-and-drop from moving text to copying text.
 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts:** MS Word includes various shortcuts like Ctrl + C (copy), Ctrl + X (cut), and Ctrl + V (paste) for editing tasks.
 
• **Reorganizing Content:** Dragging and Ctrl + dragging are practical tools for reorganizing content in lengthy documents efficiently.
 
• **Visual Cue:** While dragging, the cursor changes shape (e.g., a small box with text) to indicate whether the action is moving or copying the text.

questions.question: What happens when you press the Delete key after selecting a file in File Explorer in Windows OS?

options.text: The file is sent to the Recycle Bin.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The file is sent to the Recycle Bin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a file is deleted using the **Delete key** in File Explorer of Windows OS, it is not permanently erased but instead moved to the **Recycle Bin**.
 
• The Recycle Bin acts as a temporary storage, allowing users to **restore deleted files** if needed.
 
• The file remains in the Recycle Bin until it is **manually emptied** or the user chooses to permanently delete the file.
 
• To bypass the Recycle Bin and permanently delete a file, users can press **Shift + Delete** instead of just Delete.
 
• Deleting files temporarily through the Recycle Bin ensures **safety against accidental deletion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Recycle Bin**

 
 
• The Recycle Bin is a special folder in Windows OS used to temporarily store deleted files and folders.
 
• Files in the Recycle Bin can be restored to their original location or permanently deleted.
 
• Users can configure the Recycle Bin settings to adjust the **maximum storage capacity** or disable it entirely.
 
 
 
• **Permanently Deleting Files**
 
 
• To permanently delete a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin, users can use **Shift + Delete**.
 
• Permanently deleted files cannot be recovered through the Recycle Bin.
 
 
 
• **File Explorer**
 
 
• File Explorer is a built-in tool in Windows OS used for navigating and managing files and folders.
 
• Users can perform actions such as copying, moving, deleting, and renaming files using File Explorer.
 
 
 
• **Restoring Files**
 
 
• Files deleted and moved to the Recycle Bin can be restored by right-clicking the file and selecting **Restore**.
 
• Restored files return to their original location before deletion.

questions.question: In a multitasking operating system, what role does RAM primarily play when multiple applications are open simultaneously?

options.text: It processes user input commands from external devices like keyboard or mouse
It queues printing tasks before they reach the printer.
It temporarily holds active program data and instructions to enable fast switching between tasks.
It acts as permanent storage for installed software.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It temporarily holds active program data and instructions to enable fast switching between tasks.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)** is a volatile memory that temporarily stores data and instructions required by active applications, enabling smooth multitasking.
 
• In a multitasking operating system, RAM allows **quick access to active program data**, reducing the need to repeatedly fetch data from slower storage devices like hard drives.
 
• The operating system utilizes RAM to maintain the state of multiple applications, enabling **fast switching between tasks** without delays.
 
• RAM acts as a workspace for the CPU, ensuring that active processes and threads execute efficiently and remain responsive.
 
• When RAM is insufficient for multitasking, systems may use virtual memory (paging), which is significantly slower compared to physical RAM.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Volatile Memory:**

 
 
• RAM is classified as volatile memory, meaning its contents are lost when power is turned off.
 
• This characteristic makes RAM unsuitable for permanent data storage.
 
 
 
• **Virtual Memory:**
 
 
• When physical RAM is full, operating systems use a portion of the hard drive as virtual memory.
 
• Virtual memory is slower than RAM but ensures the system can handle more applications simultaneously.
 
 
 
• **Multitasking in Operating Systems:**
 
 
• Multitasking allows multiple applications or processes to run concurrently by sharing CPU and RAM resources.
 
• Efficient multitasking relies heavily on the speed and capacity of RAM.
 
 
 
• **Cache Memory:**
 
 
• Cache memory is a smaller, faster type of memory located closer to the CPU than RAM.
 
• It stores frequently accessed data to speed up processing tasks further.
 
 
 
• **Permanent Storage vs RAM:**
 
 
• Permanent storage devices like hard drives and SSDs retain data even after power is turned off.
 
• RAM, on the other hand, is temporary storage designed for speed and accessibility during active processes.

questions.question: Article 45 under the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution, provides for

options.text: Rights of minorities to establish educational institutions
Education for weaker sections of the country
Giving financial assistance to less advanced states

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Free and compulsory primary education**__**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **Article 45 under Directive Principles of State Policy** laid down the foundation stone of **free and compulsory education in the country**. The article states that “** **the state shall endeavour to provide, within a period of ten years from the commencement of this constitution, for **free and compulsory education for all children until they complete the age of fourteen years**”. **Article 45 recognizes the child’s right to get an education and directs the state: **
 
• To make primary education compulsory and available to all;
 
• To encourage the development of different forms of secondary education, including general and vocational education, make them accessible and available to every child,** **and take appropriate measures such as the** **introduction of free education and offering financial assistance in case of need.
 
• Equality of educational** **opportunity** **can not be denied to anyone under **Article 29(2) **according to which **admission cannot be refused to anyone on the basis of race, caste, the language** in any institution maintained by the state or aided by the state.
 
• Also, the** five articles - 15, 29(2), 15(3), 46 and 29(l) **entrust the** responsibility of equalization of educational opportunity i**n all parts of the country to the Government of India and to that end, to give special assistance to backward areas or states.
 
• It is therefore clear that the task of** **providing universal educational opportunity to all children of the country is the **joint responsibility** of the central government, state governments, and local bodies as well as voluntary organizations.
 
• The central government, in respect of primary education, has some important roles to play such as initiating researches and pilot projects in elementary education, providing financial assistance to states, acting as a coordinating agency between state and other international agencies, and sorting out the differences between various states, ensuring equitable distribution of resources and inequality of opportunities, etc. 

**Hence, we conclude that Article 45 under the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution, provides for ​Free and compulsory primary education.**

• RIMES was established in collaboration with the **United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCAP)** in **2009** after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami.

questions.question: Which of the following characters is NOT allowed in a filename when renaming in Windows?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**? (question mark)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **question mark (?)** is one of the characters prohibited in filenames in Windows operating systems.
 
• Other restricted characters include **\ / : * ? " |**, as these are reserved for system functions or file path navigation.
 
• Windows uses these special characters to perform certain operations, such as separating directories (**/**) or indicating a wildcard (*****).
 
• If you attempt to include a restricted character while renaming a file, Windows will display an error message preventing the action.
 
• These restrictions are enforced to ensure compatibility and avoid conflicts within the file system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Filename Restrictions in Windows:**

 
 
• Windows filenames cannot exceed 255 characters, including the file path.
 
• Filenames cannot end with a period (**.**) or a space (** **).
 
• Reserved names like **CON, AUX, NUL, COM1** to **COM9**, and **LPT1** to **LPT9** are also prohibited.
 
 
 
• **Wildcard Characters:**
 
 
• Wildcards like ***** and **?** are used to represent multiple or single characters in searches.
 
• Including these in filenames can interfere with file search or system commands.
 
 
 
• **File Path Syntax:**
 
 
• Windows uses **\** as a directory separator, distinguishing file paths.
 
• Other characters like **:** are reserved for drives (e.g., **C:\**).
 
 
 
• **Cross-Platform Compatibility:**
 
 
• Some characters allowed in other operating systems (e.g., Linux) may still be prohibited in Windows.
 
• Developers often avoid restricted characters to ensure portability across platforms.

questions.question: In the 2025 Uttarakhand flash flood that occurred on 5 August 2025, which Himalayan village on the route to Gangotri Dham was devastated by a torrent of water, mud and debris?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharali in Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dharali village**, located in the **Uttarkashi district** of **Uttarakhand**, witnessed a devastating flash flood on **5 August 2025**. The event was triggered by intense **cloudbursts** in the higher reaches of the **Himalayas**, causing the **Kheer Ganga** rivulet to overflow with immense force.
 
• The village is a significant transit point situated on the **Gangotri National Highway (NH-34)**, approximately **20 kilometers** before the **Gangotri Dham**. It is famous for its **apple orchards** and its proximity to the **Bhagirathi River**.
 
• The **2025 flash flood** caused a massive torrent of **water, mud, and debris** to sweep through the settlement, leading to the burial of several houses and the blockage of the **National Highway**. This disaster disrupted the **Char Dham Yatra**, leaving hundreds of pilgrims stranded.
 
• Historically, **Dharali** and surrounding areas like **Harsil** have been vulnerable to such ecological disturbances due to their **geographical location** in the **High Himalayan zone**, where steep slopes and loose soil contribute to rapid **debris flows** during monsoon seasons.
 
• **Joshimath** is located in the **Chamoli district** and is primarily known for **land subsidence** issues rather than being on the direct route to **Gangotri Dham**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Balta** is a village in the **Almora district**, which is part of the **Kumaon division**, whereas the flood occurred in the **Garhwal division**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Rudraprayag** is a district headquarters at the confluence of the **Alaknanda** and **Mandakini** rivers, serving as the gateway to **Kedarnath**, not the specific village devastated on the **Gangotri** route in this context. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uttarkashi District:** Established on **24 February 1960**, it is one of the northernmost districts of **India**, sharing an international border with **Tibet (China)**. It houses the origins of the **Ganga (at Gangotri)** and **Yamuna (at Yamunotri)** rivers.
 
• **Gangotri Dham:** One of the four sites in the **Chota Char Dham** pilgrimage. The temple is dedicated to **Goddess Ganga** and is located at an elevation of **3,100 meters**. The region is ecologically sensitive and falls under the **Gangotri National Park** administration.
 
• **Cloudburst Dynamics:** A **cloudburst** is an extreme amount of precipitation in a short period (usually exceeding **100 mm per hour**). In the **Himalayas**, these are frequent during the **monsoon months** (**July to September**) due to the orographic lifting of moisture-laden winds.
 
• **Harsil Valley:** Located very close to **Dharali**, **Harsil** is known as the "**Mini Switzerland of India**." It sits at an altitude of **2,620 meters** and is inhabited by the **Bhotia tribe**. The area is critical for **border security** and **tourism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Disaster Management:** Following the **2025 flood**, the **State Disaster Response Force (SDRF)** and **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** conducted extensive operations. Under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, the district administration is empowered to evacuate vulnerable zones.
 
• **Geological Vulnerability:** The **Main Central Thrust (MCT)** passes through the **Uttarkashi** region, making it seismically active (Zone V) and prone to **landslides**. The **1991 Uttarkashi earthquake** (magnitude **6.8**) remains one of the most significant tectonic events in this area.
 
• **National Highway 34:** This highway connects **Rishikesh** to **Gangotri**. Constant maintenance is required due to the fragile **shale and schist** rock formations that frequently collapse during heavy rains.
 
• **Ecological Impact:** The accumulation of **debris** in the **Bhagirathi River** can lead to the formation of temporary **artificial lakes**, which pose a downstream threat of **Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOF)** or flash floods if the blockages burst suddenly.
